questions.question: What does correlation measure in paired numerical data?
choices: The direction and strength of a linear association
Proof of a causal effect
The difference between two means
The total number of points

questions.question: What is the possible range of correlation coefficient r?
choices: 0 to 1 only
−1 to 1

questions.question: What does positive correlation indicate?
choices: One variable causes the other to increase
Every point has positive coordinates
Larger values of one variable tend to accompany larger values of the other
The two means are equal

questions.question: What does negative correlation indicate?
choices: All observations are negative
Larger values of one variable tend to accompany smaller values of the other
Both variables decrease over time in every case
The variables have no association

questions.question: Which r-value indicates the strongest linear association?
What does a least-squares regression line minimize?
choices: The sum of all x-values
The largest y-value
The horizontal distance between every pair of points
The sum of squared vertical residuals

questions.question: In a regression model ŷ = a + bx, what does b represent?
choices: The observed y-value for every point
The predicted y-value when x = 0
The predicted change in y for each unit increase in x
The correlation coefficient in every case

questions.question: Why does correlation not establish causation?
choices: Correlation can only be negative
A third variable or other explanation may account for the association
Regression lines cannot use real data
A causal relationship always has r = 1

questions.question: For ŷ = 4 + 2x, what is the predicted y when x = 6?
What does an r-value near zero rule out most directly?
choices: Every possible nonlinear association
Any variation in x
Any variation in y
A strong linear association

questions.question: Why can an outlier change a correlation or fitted line substantially?
choices: Outliers are excluded automatically from every calculation
One outlier forces r to zero
It may strongly affect the pattern and calculation
Outliers always make the slope positive

questions.question: What does r² = 0.64 mean in a simple least-squares regression with an intercept?
choices: 64% of y is caused by x
64% of the variation in y is accounted for by the fitted linear relationship
64% of predictions are exactly correct
The slope is 0.64

questions.question: Why is prediction outside the observed x-range called extrapolation?
choices: It extends the model beyond the data used to fit it
It repeats an observed y-value
It replaces numerical data with categories
It always gives the exact outcome

questions.question: A fitted line predicts price in dollars from size in square meters and has slope 120. What are the slope's units?
choices: Square meters per dollar
Dollars squared
Square meters squared
Dollars per square meter

questions.question: How does changing centimeters to meters for all x-values affect correlation r?
choices: It divides r by 100
It multiplies r by 100
It leaves r unchanged
It reverses the sign of r

questions.question: Ice-cream sales and swimming activity rise together in summer. Which conclusion is justified?
choices: Ice-cream purchases must cause swimming
Warm weather may influence both, so the association alone does not prove causation
Swimming must cause every ice-cream purchase
The association is impossible because neither variable is negative

questions.question: A model ŷ = 50 − 3x predicts remaining fuel from travel time. What does its negative slope mean?
choices: Predicted fuel decreases by 3 units per time unit
Time decreases by 50 for each fuel unit
Fuel always starts at −3
Correlation must equal −1 exactly

questions.question: If r = −0.8, what is r²?
Why should an intercept be interpreted cautiously when x = 0 is outside the observed range?
choices: Intercepts are never part of linear equations
A zero input makes every model undefined
It may describe an unsupported extrapolation
An intercept must always equal the smallest observed y

questions.question: A scatterplot has a strong U-shaped pattern but r is close to zero. What is the best conclusion?
choices: The variables are necessarily unrelated
There may be a strong nonlinear association
The data must contain an error
A linear model is certainly ideal
